_comment: Layout contracts for the sections that would be worst to ship broken.
These exist because of a real failure. The 'Sambal Tina 101' primer shipped
with no CSS at all — its rules lived in a stylesheet no page linked — and
every check in the repository passed. Contrast measures painted text,
responsive measures overflow, and unstyled text is usually still legible
and still fits. Nothing was watching for a section that had simply lost its
styling and fallen back to browser defaults.
So each entry states the few structural facts that separate a laid-out
section from a stack of defaults: what it lays out AS, how many columns it
resolves to, and whether its children actually sit beside each other.
Deliberately NOT asserted: pixel sizes, colours, fonts, spacing, or
screenshots. Those change constantly for good reasons and would turn this
into noise that gets ignored — which is worse than no check. Everything
here is a property that only changes when something is genuinely broken.
'display' is the sharpest tool in the box: a <span> is inline until CSS says
otherwise, and a <div> is block. An element that is supposed to be a grid
and reports 'block' has lost its rules. That is exactly what the primer did.

contracts.section: Sambal Tina 101 primer — the section that shipped unstyled

contracts.note: a <span> is inline by default; block is only true when the CSS loaded

contracts.section: Sambal Tina 101 — the three core vowels
contracts.note: unstyled this reads as the single run-together word AIO
another <span> that depends entirely on CSS to become a heading
the hub is composed rather than tiled: this theme promotes one article to reading size with its companions stacked beside it. Losing the shape rules puts it back to an undifferentiated row.

contracts.section: Discover hub — the Binabayani cultural feature
contracts.note: a single-article theme drawn as image beside copy. If this ever reports one column at desktop the feature has collapsed into an ordinary card and the theme is a lonely tile again.

contracts.section: Discover hub — the power plant wide feature
Discover hub — the power plant photograph at full measure
contracts.note: this subject is physically large and the picture is the argument, so it takes the whole measure. Dropping to one grid track would shrink it to a third and nothing else here would notice.
below 600px the hero stops being a picture with words on it and stacks
the three-track row is the whole design; one track at desktop means it collapsed

contracts.section: Marketplace logo, the dominant element in a row
contracts.note: if this stops being a sized box the mark collapses to its intrinsic size
a filter row that stops being a row stacks three chips down the page
a <span> that is only a heading because CSS says so

contracts.section: Homepage hero frame — the whole photograph, in flow
contracts.note: the frame used to be position:absolute and inset over a viewport-height band, which is what cropped the picture. It is now in normal flow at the photograph's own height. Absolute here again would mean the crop is back.

contracts.section: Homepage hero photograph — native ratio, nothing cut
contracts.note: the source is 1672x941. Rendered at its own ratio the width is about 1.777 times the height; anything else means a fixed height or an aspect-ratio has been reintroduced and the frame is being cropped again.
